note: The fuzz input after the first selector byte is copied as an IRC line. The candidate line starts with message tags and sets tag time to a lone backslash before the IRC tag-field space separator.
With selector byte zero the harness forwards the line without adding a prefix; the line still begins with '@time=\ PING'.
The IRC parser sees '@' and stores a pointer to the message-tag field, beginning at time=\.
The parser accepts the tag field and terminates it at the space without checking whether the final tag-value byte is a dangling escape.
The parsed line has tags, so the tag-processing signal path runs.
Splitting the tag key/value allocates kv[1] as a string whose complete contents are the single backslash byte followed by its terminator.
The allocated tag value containing only a lone escape is passed to the unescape routine.

When the first and only value byte is backslash, tmp is advanced to the string terminator inside the branch; the for-loop increment then advances it past the terminator and parsing continues outside the tag value.
